style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: Luther's psalm -- 'A Mighty Fortress' was forged from this furnace -- and the church's song for the day the world comes apart. Three stanzas, each sealed with Selah. First, the unshakable confidence: God is refuge and strength, a help proved present in trouble, so that even if the earth gives way and the mountains topple into the heart of the sea -- creation itself un-creating -- we will not fear. Second, the contrast of waters: against the roaring, foaming chaos-sea stands a quiet river whose channels gladden the city of God; she is not moved, because God is in her midst, and His help arrives at the turning of the morning. Nations rage and kingdoms totter with the same verb the mountains used, and one utterance of His voice melts the earth. Third, the invitation to survey the battlefield after He has ended the battle: bows snapped, spears cut apart, chariots burned -- and then the voice from the center of it all: 'Be still -- let your hands drop -- and know that I am God.' The refrain answers twice, the whole gospel in a couplet: the LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our high fortress.

1.text: For the choir director. Of the sons of Korah, a song set for soprano voices. God is our refuge and strength, a help in trouble proved thoroughly present.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] for the sons [ben] of Korah [Qorach], A Song [shir] upon Alamoth [alamoth -- maidens' voices, the high register]. God [Elohim] is our refuge [machseh -- shelter] and strength [oz], a very [meod] present [matsa -- found, proved findable] help [ezrah] in trouble [tsarah].
1.notes: machseh (H4268) is the shelter you run to, oz (H5797) the strength that meets you there. 'Very present' is literally 'found exceedingly' -- matsa (H4672): in tsarah (H6869) He has been looked for and found, every time. Alamoth (H5961) suggests high voices: thunder scored for sopranos.

2.text: Therefore we will not fear, though the earth gives way and the mountains topple into the heart of the sea,
2.amp: Therefore will not we fear [yare], though the earth [eretz] be removed [mur -- changed, gives way], and though the mountains [har] be carried [mot -- totter, slip] into the midst ['heart of the seas', leb yam, the KJV margin];
2.notes: The scenario is un-creation: the harim (H2022), Scripture's emblem of permanence, sliding into the leb yam (H3820, H3220), the heart of the seas -- Genesis 1 running backward. 'Therefore' hangs all fearlessness on verse 1; the ground may fail, the Refuge cannot.

3.text: though the waters of it roar and boil into foam, though the mountains shake at its swelling pride. Selah.
3.amp: Though the waters [mayim] thereof roar [hamah] and be troubled [chamar -- boil, foam], though the mountains [har] shake [raash] with the swelling [gaavah -- the pride] thereof. Selah [selah].
3.notes: gaavah (H1346) is pride: the sea swells with arrogance, chaos strutting. hamah (H1993) is the same roar that churned the downcast soul of Psalm 42:5 -- outer and inner storms share one vocabulary, and the psalm answers both.

4.text: There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God, the holy dwelling place of the Most High.
4.amp: There is a river [nahar], the streams [peleg -- channels] whereof shall make glad [samach] the city [ir] of God [Elohim], the holy [qadosh] place of the tabernacles [mishkan -- dwelling places] of the most High [Elyon].
4.notes: Against the roaring sea, a quiet nahar (H5104): Jerusalem has no great river -- the city's gladness flows from God's presence itself, the stream Eden had (cf. Genesis 2:10) and the New Jerusalem will have again (cf. Revelation 22:1). peleg (H6388) is the irrigation-channel of Psalm 1:3: steady water, not spectacular water.

5.text: God is in the midst of her; she will not be toppled. God will help her at the turning of the morning.
5.amp: God [Elohim] is in the midst [qereb] of her; she shall not be moved [mot]: God shall help [azar] her, and that right early ['when the morning appeareth', boqer, the KJV margin].
5.notes: The verse hands the mountains' verb to the city and negates it: the harim mot (H4131), totter, in verse 2; she shall NOT mot, because Elohim is in her qereb (H7130), her inmost center. Help 'at the turn of the boqer' (H1242) -- God's cavalry has a habit of arriving at dawn (cf. Exodus 14:27).

6.text: Nations raged, kingdoms tottered; He lifted His voice, and the earth melted away.
6.amp: The heathen [goy -- the nations] raged [hamah], the kingdoms [mamlakah] were moved [mot]: He uttered [natan -- gave forth] His voice [qol], the earth [eretz] melted [mug].
6.notes: The chaos-sea resolves into its real referent: goyim (H1471) hamah, nations roaring like the waters of verse 3, mamlakot (H4467) tottering like the mountains. Against all of it, one qol (H6963): He speaks, and the solid earth goes soft -- mug (H4127), melted like wax.

7.text: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our high fortress. Selah.
7.amp: The LORD [YHWH] of hosts [tsaba -- of Armies] is with us; the God [Elohim] of Jacob [Yaaqob] is our refuge ['an high place for us', misgab, the KJV margin]. Selah [selah].
7.notes: The refrain: YHWH tsebaoth (H3068, H6635), commander of every army seen and unseen, is Immanu -- WITH us, the Immanuel-word (cf. Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23). And He is the God of Jacob, the schemer He never abandoned: grace-history as guarantee. misgab (H4869) is the unscalable height.

8.text: Come, gaze on the works of the LORD, the desolations He has laid across the earth.
8.amp: Come [yalak], behold [chazah -- gaze as a seer] the works [miphalot] of the LORD [YHWH], what desolations [shammah] He has made [sum] in the earth [eretz].
8.notes: chazah (H2372), the seer's beholding: a guided tour of the morning after. The shammah (H8047), the desolations, are God's -- but the next verse shows what He desolated: not cities, but the weapons that besieged them.

9.text: He makes wars cease to the end of the earth; He snaps the bow and cuts the spear in two; He burns the war-wagons in the fire.
9.amp: He makes wars [milchamah] to cease [shabat -- rest, stop] unto the end [qatseh] of the earth [eretz]; He breaks [shabar] the bow [qeshet], and cuts [qatsats] the spear [chanit] in sunder; He burns [saraph] the chariot [agalah] in the fire [esh].
9.notes: shabat (H7673): He sabbaths the wars -- forces the fighting to rest. The disarmament is itemized: qeshet snapped, chanit chopped, chariots to the esh (H784). The prophets carry the scene forward to swords beaten into plowshares (cf. Isaiah 2:4; Micah 4:3).

10.text: 'Let go, be still, and know that I am God. Among the nations I will be exalted; in all the earth I will be exalted.'
10.amp: Be still [raphah -- let go, drop the hands, cease striving], and know [yada] that I am God [Elohim]: I will be exalted [rum] among the heathen [goy], I will be exalted in the earth [eretz].
10.notes: raphah (H7503) is literally to let the hands drop -- addressed first to the warring nations (stand down), and through them to every clenched believer. The stillness is not emptiness but yada (H3045): knowing WHO holds the field. The double 'I will be rum (H7311)' is history's fixed outcome, announced from its center.

11.text: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our high fortress. Selah.
11.amp: The LORD [YHWH] of hosts [tsaba] is with us; the God [Elohim] of Jacob [Yaaqob] is our refuge [misgab -- our high fortress]. Selah [selah].
11.notes: The refrain sealed a second time, now with verse 10 ringing inside it: the God who commands stillness is the God who stands with. Luther sang it against empires -- 'a mighty fortress', ein feste Burg, is this misgab -- and the church has held the line with it ever since.
